documents.title: Service appointment confirmed
documents.text:
To: Hannah Wu
From: Redline Auto Care
Date: February 6

Dear Hannah Wu,
Your appointment for a 60,000-km service is confirmed for Tuesday, February 13, at 8:30 a.m. at our Eastgate location. The service includes an oil change, brake inspection, tire rotation, and a 30-point safety check, with a total estimated cost of $320. If additional repairs are needed, a technician will call you for approval before any work begins. Please remove valuables from your car and leave the key at the front desk. A free shuttle to the Eastgate business park is available, or you can wait in our lounge, which has free Wi-Fi. The work normally takes about three hours. Reply to this e-mail if you need to reschedule.

documents.title: Greenfield Expands Recycling Program
documents.text: GREENFIELD (April 18) - Greenfield residents will soon be able to recycle more types of waste at the curb. [A] Beginning June 3, the city will collect food scraps and yard waste in addition to paper, glass, and plastic, using a new brown bin that will be delivered to each household in May. [B] Public Works director Jerome Bell said the program aims to reduce the amount of garbage sent to the landfill by one third within two years. [C] Residents who prefer not to use the service may opt out, but they will continue to pay the monthly waste fee of $18. [D] Information sessions will be held at the library on April 25 and May 9, and a guide in six languages is available online.

questions.prompt: What change is described in the article?
choices: The city will collect more kinds of waste for recycling
questions.explanation: Food scraps and yard waste will be added to curbside collection.

questions.prompt: How will households receive the brown bin?
choices: It will be delivered to their homes in May
They can pick it up at the library
It will arrive with the first pickup in June
questions.explanation: The new bin will be delivered to each household in May.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about residents who opt out?
choices: They will still be charged the waste fee
questions.explanation: They will continue to pay the monthly fee of $18.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "The brown bins will be emptied every Monday."
questions.explanation: The sentence follows the one introducing the new brown bin and the June 3 start of collection.

documents.title: Dispute of a September electricity bill
documents.text:
Dear Customer Service,
I am writing about my electricity bill for September (account 3317-82). The bill shows a charge of $286, which is more than double my usual amount of about $120. I have not changed my habits, and no one has been staying at my home. I asked for a meter reading on September 29, but the technician did not arrive on the appointed day and was never rescheduled. I believe the charge is based on an estimated reading. Please send someone to read the meter and correct the bill. Until this matter is resolved, I will pay only the usual amount.
I look forward to your prompt reply.
Sincerely,
Carlos Rivera

questions.explanation: He questions a charge that is more than double his usual bill.

questions.prompt: What does Carlos Rivera think caused the high charge?
choices: An estimate instead of a real meter reading
questions.explanation: He believes the charge is based on an estimated reading.

questions.prompt: What does Carlos Rivera plan to pay for now?
questions.explanation: He will pay only the usual amount until the matter is resolved.

documents.title: Harborview Hotel: Meeting Packages
documents.text:
Half-day package (4 hours): $45 per person. Includes meeting room, projector, and coffee break.
Full-day package (8 hours): $75 per person. Adds a lunch buffet and an afternoon snack.
Overnight package: $145 per person. Adds a standard single room and breakfast.

Minimum 10 participants. Rooms: Cedar (up to 20 people), Birch (up to 40), Grand Hall (up to 120). Groups of 30 or more receive a 10 percent discount on the total. The final headcount is due 7 days before the event.

documents.title: Next year's budget requests
documents.text:
TO: Department managers
FROM: Lucas Fenn, Chief Financial Officer
DATE: October 7
SUBJECT: Next year's budget requests

Budget requests for the next fiscal year must be submitted by November 1 through the finance portal. Each request must include a justification and, for any purchase above $5,000, two vendor quotes. Departments should aim to hold overall spending at this year's level; requests for increases will be approved only if they directly support revenue growth. Hiring requests must be submitted separately to Human Resources. Budget review meetings will take place the week of November 11.

documents.title: City Pool to Reopen After Renovation
documents.text: RIVERTON (May 20) - The Riverton Community Pool will reopen on June 8 after a six-month renovation. The $2.4 million project added a heated children's pool, a new filtration system, and improved accessibility, including a lift for swimmers with limited mobility. Annual passes will cost $90 for adults and $50 for children; day passes remain $6. Residents who held a pass before the closure will receive an e-mail with a free one-month extension. Swimming lessons for ages 4 to 12 begin June 17.

documents.title: Employee Parking Permit Renewal
documents.text: Annual parking permits expire on December 31. Renewal for next year is $240 for the covered garage and $120 for the open lot. Employees who renew before December 1 receive a 10 percent discount. Payroll deduction is available in 12 monthly installments. New applicants are placed on a waiting list for the covered garage; open-lot permits are issued immediately. Lost permits can be replaced for $15 at the Security Office in Building A, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
